subtitle: Adversarial science digests — a thesis defended and attacked to a verdict, every claim backed by computation.

disputes.title: A Conveyor Running Empty
disputes.subtitle: Imaging shows tracer pouring into perivascular spaces, and it is tempting to read that influx as a meter of how much solute the brain clears. But if the rate-limiting step is interstitial exchange or vascular egress rather than the imaged conduit, influx and net clearance come apart. In a steady-state series-conductance model holding a neutral Peclet substrate, a physiologically plausible egress bottleneck drops the influx-clearance Spearman correlation from 0.51 across the full plausible box to 0.04.
disputes.verdict: CON prevailed on argumentation, and within scope the claim was not supported. In a steady-state series-conductance model holding the neutral Peclet substrate, the full plausible box gives a Spearman influx-clearance correlation of only 0.51, and a physiologically plausible vascular-egress or interstitial-exchange bottleneck drops it to 0.04 (below the registered 0.30 reject line and far short of the 0.80 pass bar), while a conduit-limited regime keeps the proxy near-perfect (1.00). Bounded to synthetic substrates; the in vivo decisive test remains unresolved.

disputes.title: Controllable, or Just Well-Connected?
disputes.subtitle: Network control theory promises that a node's controllability tells you which parts of the brain are the levers. On synthetic connectomes built to favour that claim — including ones with planted bridging hubs — controllability turns out to be node strength wearing a costume: it re-ranks almost nothing.
disputes.verdict: CON prevailed on argumentation, and within scope the claim was not supported. On a thesis-friendly modular connectome with planted connector hubs, adding average and modal controllability moved held-out hub ranking by -0.0003 AUC (95% CI [-0.0019, +0.0026], inside the +/-0.02 reject band, far short of the registered +0.05 bar); controllability is rank-redundant with strength (Spearman 0.937 / -0.934; top-30 overlap 21/30) and a degree-preserving null reproduces the non-effect. Bounded to synthetic substrates; the real-data version remains untested.

disputes.title: When the Detector Catches Its Own Shadow
disputes.subtitle: Is a standard avalanche power-law + crackling pipeline a diagnostic detector of network criticality, or a measurement that cries 'critical' at matched subcritical noise?
disputes.verdict: CON prevailed on argumentation and on the merits. At literature-typical sample sizes a fully validated avalanche power-law + crackling pipeline raised false positives of 0.39-0.47 on a matched subcritical control — above its own registered 0.20 falsifier — while the critical positive control passed (TPR 0.82-0.98); the false-positive rate met the 0.05 diagnostic target only at n>=2500. Synthetic branching model, not real cortical data.

disputes.title: When Triple Correlations Fall Silent
disputes.subtitle: A frozen sparse-limit claim that coskewness leakage hijacks a pairwise model's 'explained entropy' until the number means nothing, stress-tested on exactly-enumerable binary ensembles: can a third-order moment move a yardstick built from first and second moments?
disputes.verdict: CON: the strong sparse-limit claim is not supported. The pairwise MaxEnt explained entropy S1-S2 is a function of first and second moments only, so coskewness cannot make it higher-order while those moments are fixed; and in a standard dichotomized-Gaussian sparse family the higher-order fraction stays below 0.06 down to p~0.005 rather than rising to 1.

disputes.title: The Song and the Strange Attractor
disputes.subtitle: Can a stereotyped neural sequence be the signature of deterministic chaos with a positive Lyapunov exponent -- or does a stable, noise-driven adaptation chain reproduce the same phenomenology while the timing precision forbids the chaotic source?
disputes.verdict: CON prevailed and was right on the merits: on synthetic models calibrated to zebra-finch HVC, a stable adaptation-clocked chain reproduces rigid order and low-CV variable timing (CV 0.080, 0 errors) with no positive Lyapunov exponent, while sub-millisecond timing precision plus the saddle-exit identity Var(tau)=Var(ln|z|)/lambda^2 and a mean/CV lambda-lock show a positive exponent would be an amplifier of noise, not its source. The strong chaotic-itinerancy thesis is unsupported on the flagship example; the seed paper's existence result is untouched.

disputes.title: Two Roads to One Number
disputes.subtitle: Is the cortex's near-1/n representation spectrum the fingerprint of a single tunable regime — one causal knob α(λ_max), soft supercriticality — or can two unrelated roads reach the same exponent?
disputes.verdict: Aramis (CON) prevailed and was right on the merits: the strong hypothesis — a single causal knob α(λ_max) displacing the stimulus-geometry account — does not survive a toy counterexample where α≈1 is reachable subcritically (λ_max<0) via power-law input geometry. Within a fixed ensemble α does move monotonically with λ_max, but that is a property of the toy reservoir, not a cortical finding.

disputes.title: A Ghost Made of Timing
disputes.subtitle: Is a brain co-skewness signal that foundation models 'forgot' a real instantaneous three-way mechanism, or just the static shadow of timing the analysis never modelled?
disputes.verdict: PRO prevailed on argumentation; substantively unclear. A lagged, shared, skewed driver is sufficient to make static co-skewness predict cognition while a directed lagged-FC baseline absorbs it almost entirely (increment ~0.00 in the bundle); but synthetic sufficiency does not establish that real fMRI lives in that regime.

disputes.title: The Yardstick That Shrank
disputes.subtitle: Does a method that compresses data to gain power secretly confirm too-simple theories — or does it just depend on where you measure the bar?
disputes.verdict: Aramis wins: the strong thesis fails — under an honest full-space noise ceiling the false-confirmation rate is 0% at every rank; the apparent inflation was an artifact of estimating the ceiling in the compressed space.

disputes.title: Two Choirs in the Dark
disputes.subtitle: Can a shared external signal be told from weak mutual coupling by passive observation alone?
